sections.heading: Life and writing.
paragraphs: Mrinmoy Kumar Nath combines poetry with a professional background in dentistry in Assam. His journal biography places him in Mangaldoi and describes work as a lyricist as well as a poet. Reports of literary gatherings also connect his name with Assam’s wider poetry and cultural community.

His two Kabita Live contributions approach departure on different scales. ‘If I go away’ moves from reproach towards the shared memory left by a relationship. ‘If I die’ asks whether a death in the service of one’s country awakens courage or leaves only fear. Their direct language and conditional openings turn absence into a question addressed to those who remain.

sections.heading: Life and writing.
paragraphs: Monalisa Dash Dwibedy writes poetry in Odia and English, alongside travel essays for OdishaPlus. Her books include the English collection ‘Pearls of Strawberry Moon’. A background in IT consulting sits beside a literary interest in landscape and inward reflection; in her travel writing, places are encountered through affection, remembered sensations and the lives around them.

Her Odia poem ‘ଈଶ୍ବର’ (‘God’) in Kabita Live turns a spiritual figure into a witness to the pressures of the present. Heat, cyclones, urbanisation and the appetite for power make the search for a compassionate heart increasingly difficult. The poem’s repeated return to God gives its social questions a searching rhythm, ending with an absence within human hearts rather than a distant heaven.

sections.heading: Life and writing.
paragraphs: Misna Chanu writes poetry in Manipuri and English and also works as an editor and translator. Originally from Assam, she is described in her literary biography as based in Gurgaon. Her books include A Little Piece of Melancholic Sky, Many Shades of Love and The Silent Whispers, alongside the children’s book Once Upon a Time.

In her Kabita Live poems, love becomes a landscape carried within the self. Your Existence gathers the beloved into rain, seasons, dreams and remembered music. Oasis offers a quieter encounter: the speaker finds a familiar homeland in another being, yet leaves its water untouched, taking away only the fragrance of memory. Together, the poems hold affection close without making possession its measure.

sections.heading: Life and writing.
paragraphs: Mukul Kumar is a poet, novelist and civil servant from the 1997 batch of the Indian Railway Traffic Service. His writing includes the English poetry collection The Irrepressible Echoes and the novel As Boys Become Men, which follows young men preparing for the civil services. His Kabita Live contributions bring English and Hindi into the same body of work.

These poems move between inward struggle and the lives that public achievement can overlook. Many Lives, Many Deaths balances abundance against disappearance through clouds, rain and breath. In बेरुह पैरहन, a labourer helps build a civilisation whose outward form lacks a living soul. A Redeeming Duel turns to Sisyphus and Shakespeare to keep a difficult argument with despair open to the possibility of another day.

sources.label: Rupa Publications — As Boys Become Men

sections.heading: Life and writing.
paragraphs: Minu Verma’s Hindi poems in Kabita Live range from the small ceremonies of evening to the vulnerability of a neglected mother. In गोधूलि, wind, birds, leaves and flowers prepare the meeting of day and night; the sun’s departure makes room for the moon and waiting stars.

कौन हैं वो..? gives that attention to a woman left alone by the family she once sustained. Its repeated question gradually reveals a mother whose care has gone unreturned. जीवन जंग नही takes another direction, asking its reader to recognise flowers among the thorns and to keep moving through darkness and storms. Across these poems, care appears both as something people need and as a way of facing the world.

sections.heading: Life and writing.
paragraphs: Manua Das, also known as Manoranjan Das, is an Odia poet and translator whose work extends to filmmaking, scripts and voice performance. His poetry books include Mahufena, Kahari Akhire Nida Nahin and Antabujula. His publisher’s biography also records translations of Odia poetry and fiction into English.

His Kabita Live poem କାହିଁକି unfolds through questions addressed to an absent companion. A hand once held, a bridge between hearts and words left on paper make absence tangible. As the poem moves towards an invitation to return, sea waves, sand, sky and the currents of time carry its restless memory. Repetition gives the poem continuity while each question opens a different part of the loss.

sections.heading: Life and writing.
paragraphs: Mamata Kiran writes Hindi poetry and ghazals alongside a career in journalism and broadcasting. Her literary profile records work with newspapers and television, and as a newsreader, announcer and compere for All India Radio. Her poetry collection वृक्ष था हरा भरा belongs to a wider practice that includes articles, interviews and documentary scripts.

In her Kabita Live ghazal, the recurring नहीं देता joins couplets about guidance, shelter, trust and disappointment. A guide withholds the road; an invitation arrives without an address. Questions directed towards the divine sit beside human failures of care, while images of stars, clouds and the moon keep wonder within reach. The closing use of किरण brings the poet’s signature into this movement between questioning and light.
